study type: Prospective, double-blind, randomized, controlled, dose-finding trial
exposure: Dose of prophylactic norepinephrine (0.025, 0.05, 0.075, and 0.1 ug/kg/min vs. normal saline)
outcome: Overall stability of systolic blood pressure control
Effective dose of norepinephrine to prevent hypotension in 50% and 90% of patients
Neonatal outcomes (blood gas values and Apgar scores)
cohort: 99 pregnant women (primipara or multipara), aged 18-40 years, singleton pregnancy ≥ 37 weeks, scheduled for elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia
finding: Increasing doses of prophylactic norepinephrine infusion were associated with a decreased incidence of postspinal anesthesia hypotension in women undergoing cesarean section.
